item.title: Autoscroll
item.description:
Autoscroll is a Python and PyQt6 command-line application that turns mouse movement into horizontal and vertical scrolling. It supports configurable buttons, scroll speed, and configuration changes without restarting.

Links

  • Source code: https://github.com/alwaldend/src/tree/master/projects/autoscroll

Features

  • Platfrom-independent autoscroll
  • Config file with hot-reload
  • Some argparse tinkering
  • Python3, PyQt6

Usage

By default, the icon is disabled, to enable it pass --icon-enable

You can pass file contents as command line arguments using @path/to/the/file syntax. Arguments in that case can be placed wherever - on one line, on several lines

item.title: Autoscroll
item.description:
Autoscroll turns mouse movement into scrolling. Move the pointer and the page scrolls horizontally or vertically, with configurable buttons, speed, and a configuration that reloads without restarting.

Features

  • Horizontal and vertical scrolling driven by mouse movement
  • Configurable buttons and scroll speed
  • Configuration changes applied without a restart
  • Python and PyQt6 command-line application

item.title: MLOps 2026
item.description: An MLOps course project with a factory-based FastAPI application named recommender, served by Uvicorn. App and router instances are created inside factories. RecommenderApplication owns the app and receives its service in the constructor; RecommendationRouter owns the versioned routes and service reference. The injected RecommendationService implements __aenter__ and __aexit__ for model loading and deterministic shutdown. Its idempotent close() also runs from __del__ as a fallback. Application, router and service state is private; app and router access use explicit read-only properties. Imports do not start services or create shared application instances. Response contracts are exported from internal/models. Implementation lives under internal/recommender/, with other future apps owning sibling packages under internal/ and separate cmd/ entry points.

item.title: Py
item.description:
This package owns the repository Python dependency manifest pyproject.toml and native uv.lock. Update it with //tools/py:uv_lock.update; root //:uv_lock.update is an alias. Bazel’s pip.parse reads uv.lock directly, and Gazelle uses that same lock to validate its import manifest. There are no requirements-file exports or separately maintained pip locks.

BUILD files load lock directly from @rules_python//python/uv:lock.bzl with out = "uv.lock", which selects native uv lock. Build uv_lock to regenerate the lock without modifying source. Run uv_lock.update to replace the checked-in file, then review package versions, hashes and platform/Python markers. Extras are declared in pyproject.toml and retained in the native lock.
